purpose.description: Audit the temporal boundaries of identifiability under delayed observation.
purpose.role: Separate delay-induced estimation difficulty from genuine interface-level non-identifiability.
not_used_for: assuming longer history always restores identifiability
replacing temporal factorization analysis with prediction benchmarks

system_class.description: Dynamical systems with delayed observation access.

delay_operator.definition: Maps system trajectories to observations shifted by temporal lag tau.

audit_dimensions.question: Does the interface observe the target-relevant phase of system evolution?
Can additional history reconstruct missing temporal distinctions?
Does the target depend on hidden future trajectory branches?
audit_dimensions.result: creates ambiguity under insufficient temporal access

boundary_checks.reason: Delayed interfaces with sufficient history/interventions still satisfy factorization.
Different systems may remain observationally equivalent under the available interface.
Finite predictive success does not prove existence of a unique target mapping.

boundary_checks.claim: Delay is only an estimator problem
boundary_checks.reason: Some delays create genuine observation equivalence classes with divergent targets.

temporal_failure_modes.name: phase_aliasing
temporal_failure_modes.description: Different system phases produce identical delayed observations.

temporal_failure_modes.name: trajectory_compression
temporal_failure_modes.description: Temporal evolution collapses into insufficient historical representation.

temporal_failure_modes.name: future_branch_ambiguity
temporal_failure_modes.description: Multiple possible continuations remain consistent with delayed observations.

temporal_rank.definition: Number of target-relevant temporal distinctions preserved by the interface.

critical_boundary.finding: Delay increases interface requirements but does not determine impossibility by itself.

formal_statement.good_interface: for all f_a,f_b: O_tau(f_a)=O_tau(f_b) implies L_T(f_a)=L_T(f_b)

established: temporal delay is an interface resource constraint
delay-induced failure can be expressed through factorization failure
history and intervention can restore temporal identifiability

decision.meaning: The temporal boundary of identifiability has been characterized.
authorized_next_steps: extend to adaptive systems with changing delays

notes: The relevant resource is not time itself but preserved temporal distinctions.
Delay transforms direct observation into an interface design problem.
The factorization criterion remains unchanged across temporal regimes.
